feature: A long edit opens without freezing
summary: The hour-long reference edit opens with its longest main thread pause at about 230 ms, down from 4 s today and 135 s on 2026-11-12. The 20 minute edit's worst pause is about 185 ms and the 6 minute edit's about 170 ms. Those two are still above their 100 ms bar, so the task stays open.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. The hour-long edit is Scripts/perf/reference-edit.sh 60 (it writes and opens the project).

try.do: Run Scripts/perf/reference-edit.sh 60 --no-open, then open the project it prints with File > Open.
Click a clip on V1 as soon as the window appears.
Scroll the tracks down past the first Zoom rows, then back up.
Open the 6 minute edit the same way (reference-edit.sh 6) and watch the tracks and the panel come in.
Press Space to play, and Space again to stop.

evaluate: Does the hour-long edit's window answer your first click straight away?
When the window opens, do you notice the track rows or the panel sections landing a moment after the ruler?
Scrolling the tracks quickly, do you ever see a Zoom row empty before its bars draw?
Do V1's waveforms appear within a second or so of opening?
rough: Measured with the walk's markers down, as a person's app has none (worst pass, ms; before is today's build at the start of this task with markers up, the only way it could be measured then): 60 min 4004 -> 228 to 239; 20 min 1561 -> 184 to 185; 6 min 706 -> 171. With the markers up as before: 60 min 327, 20 min 1168, 6 min 404, most of which is the walk's own 837 hidden marker views being read for accessibility.

The 6 and 20 minute edits are still over the 100 ms bar. What is left is the window's first build (ruler, tool bar, canvas, empty panel); a plain screenshot opens with a 143 ms pass, so getting there means making every editor window cheaper to open. This task (an-hour-long-edit-opens-in-a-few-seconds-not-two) stays open for it.

Ztabby, running on this Mac, reads every new window's accessibility tree; on the hour edit that read cost 640 ms when every zoom row was built. With the zoom rows built only near the screen and the walk markers down, no such pass shows up in a 5 second wait.

Opening straight into Edit now brings the tracks' rows in a pass after the ruler, and the panel's sections a pass each after that, as switching from View to Edit already did. A video opened in Current gets the same, since the timeline files are shared.
No mock covers opening speed; nothing on screen differs from before once the window has opened.
